reasoning_traces.think:
The model employs a dual-branch architecture combining ResNet-based image processing with a lightweight Transformer for 2D skeletal features. The Fine-Grained Attention Module (FGAM) refines intra-modal features via self-attention, while the Geometric Correspondence Module (MGCM) performs cross-modal attention between image tokens and pose features. This fusion enables classification of musculoskeletal risk using REBA-based labels. However, the model's performance is compromised because REBA labels are computed deterministically from the same skeletal inputs used for training, creating a circular dependency that inflates accuracy metrics. The model essentially memorizes the rule rather than learning meaningful mappings. The failure mode arises from this label leakage, rendering the model incapable of predicting real-world injuries beyond its training domain. The geometric correspondence mechanism assumes reliable skeletal alignment, but misalignment or occlusion leads to degraded performance. Thus, despite high F1 scores and strong validation metrics, the model lacks transferability and predictive validity for practical applications such as NFL injury forecasting.
